items.title: Document-cap eviction policy lacks a safe lifecycle contract
items.statement: LSPS-027 requires a per-server open-document limit and didClose on buffer eviction, but the authoritative core does not define which buffer is evicted, whether focused, dirty, pinned, or request-active buffers are protected, how callers are notified, or how an evicted buffer is reopened and resynchronized. The cap can therefore silently invalidate server state or discard a consumer's expected semantic availability.
items.impact: Scale pressure can produce incorrect server document state, stale results, or surprise loss of LSP service for an active editor.
items.builder_discretion: Choose an eviction algorithm, but specify protected states, notification semantics, and deterministic reopen/resync behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The LSP client controls scale pressure by limiting open documents per server, sending didClose on buffer eviction, capping initialize roots, debouncing didChange at the default interval, preferring incremental contentChanges when supported, and avoiding thousands of initialize paths.

items.title: Debounced changes have no ordering or flush semantics
items.statement: The core names a 100 ms didChange debounce and incremental changes, but does not define document-version monotonicity, edit coalescing, cancellation, or mandatory flush points before hover, navigation, save, rename, formatting, close, or process failure. Concurrent requests can observe a server snapshot older than the editor snapshot.
items.impact: Requests may return positions or edits against stale content and can corrupt write-capable operations.
items.builder_discretion: Select the queue implementation, while preserving ordered versions and explicit barriers for dependent requests and shutdown.

items.title: Fallback transition and staleness truth are underdefined
items.statement: LSPS-028 assigns regex, heuristic, or indexed fallback navigation to FileManager and forbids claiming healthy LSP state, but it does not define the unavailable predicate, transition from LSP results to fallback results and back, cache invalidation, provenance labeling, or what existing Problems and symbol views show during the transition.
items.impact: Users and callers can mistake stale or heuristic results for current semantic-server results.
items.builder_discretion: Choose presentation details, but expose provenance, freshness, transition state, and invalidation behavior consistently to every consumer.

evidence.exact_quote: - Fallback symbol behavior must not claim healthy LSP diagnostics or semantic symbol state.

items.title: Optional install hints lack a trust and execution boundary
items.statement: The fallback contract preserves an optional install hint, but the core does not say who supplies it, whether it is inert text or executable UI, how package names and URLs are authenticated, which actor approves installation, or whether workspace-controlled metadata can influence it.
items.impact: A malicious workspace or server registry entry could steer a user toward an unsafe command or package under the appearance of product guidance.
items.builder_discretion: Installation may remain manual, but trust origin, escaping, consent, and prohibition on ambient execution need normative treatment.

evidence.exact_quote: - optional install hint

items.title: Stdio bridge boundary omits command, port, and process safety
items.statement: LSPS-029 permits custom stdio bridge commands and preserves auto port discovery, yet defines no command-origin or argument-escaping rules, localhost/authentication restriction, port-selection race handling, startup timeout, child-process ownership, crash detection, restart policy, or cleanup. Binary-safe buffers and Windows URI normalization are tokens rather than falsifiable contracts.
items.impact: Bridge configuration can execute unintended commands, connect to the wrong TCP listener, leak workspace data, or leave hung/orphaned processes.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the bridge implementation, but constrain command provenance, endpoint scope, lifecycle, authentication assumptions, and failure recovery.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The MVP LSP client speaks stdio only; TCP-only servers such as Godot are supported through custom stdio bridge commands like godot-lsp-stdio-bridge, while native TCP/socket support remains out of scope for MVP.

items.title: MVP native transport scope is explicit
items.statement: The core explicitly excludes native TCP/socket support from MVP and requires bridge usage, preventing an implementation from silently widening the MVP transport surface.

evidence.exact_quote: - Native TCP/socket support is out of scope for MVP.

items.title: Result envelope statuses have no payload or transition semantics
items.statement: LSPS-030 fixes four status values but does not define required result and error payloads, whether partial includes usable data and continuation metadata, how cancellation and timeout map into the envelope, or whether unavailable is retryable. Callers cannot interpret the same status consistently.
items.impact: Consumers may display partial data as complete, retry permanent failures, or lose actionable error context.
items.builder_discretion: Payload shape can vary by operation, but every status needs invariant fields and retry/display semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The canonical MVP LSP surface preserves its operation inventory, normalized parameter fields, and result status envelope using operation, query, path, position, newName, status, and the ok, partial, unavailable, or error status values.

items.title: Rename approval does not define preview, scope, freshness, or atomic recovery
items.statement: LSPS-031 correctly gates rename approval, but the core does not bind approval to an immutable edit preview, workspace and file scope, document versions, approver identity, FileSafe transaction, partial-apply behavior, or rollback. An approval can become stale between computation and application.
items.impact: A stale or overbroad rename may mutate unintended files and leave a partially applied workspace without a defined recovery path.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the preview UI, but approval must bind to exact edits and versions, then apply atomically or produce deterministic rollback evidence.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The write-capable rename operation is approval-gated, requires path, position, and newName, and treats lsp_rename as a legacy alias for rename rather than a second operation over the nine read-only operation surface.

items.title: Direct mutation is explicitly barred for rename and formatting
items.statement: The Phase 2 constraint explicitly routes rename and formatting through FileSafe-backed paths instead of direct mutation. This is a clear destructive-action boundary, although the transactional details remain outside this window.

evidence.exact_quote: - Rename and formatting use FileSafe-backed paths rather than direct mutation.

items.title: Phase 2 has no machine-readable dependency on Phase 1
items.statement: LSPS-032 describes Phase 1 as the foundation before navigation and chat enhancements, while LSPS-032 and LSPS-033 both declare empty depends_on and unblocks arrays. The phase transition is prose-only and permits Phase 2 planning or compilation without its stated foundation.
items.impact: Node-readiness and downstream consumers can treat Phase 2 as independently buildable despite missing core registry, sync, diagnostics, fallback, or status behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Encode the phase prerequisite or define feature-level dependencies that make the ordering enforceable.

evidence.exact_quote: depends_on: []

items.title: Assistant diagnostics have no privacy or data-lifecycle contract
items.statement: Phase 2 includes diagnostics for LLM/Assistant and Chat LSP, but the core does not specify consent, data minimization, redaction of source and paths, local versus remote processing, retention, deletion, tenant boundary, or whether untrusted diagnostic text may enter prompts.
items.impact: Source code, local paths, diagnostics, or adversarial server text can be disclosed or retained beyond user expectations.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the contextual payload, but define explicit consent, provenance, minimization, redaction, transmission, and retention rules.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Phase 2 adds editor navigation and editing features, inlay and semantic features, code actions and code lens, signature help, timeout/cancellation, per-server enable/disable, Settings > LSP, bridge pattern, Chat LSP, and diagnostics for Assistant/Interview context.

items.title: Status, Problems, and Settings surfaces lack accessible state semantics
items.statement: The phase outcomes name Problems integration, LSP status UI, fallback, and Settings > LSP, but provide no normative loading, disabled, degraded, stale, partial, error, or recovery presentation; no keyboard, focus, screen-reader, non-color cue, or announcement requirements; and no relationship between server state and displayed data freshness.
items.impact: Users, especially assistive-technology users, may be unable to distinguish healthy results from stale, partial, disabled, or failed LSP states.
items.builder_discretion: Choose visual styling, but expose the full state model through accessible names, roles, focus order, announcements, and non-color cues.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Phase 1 ships the core LSP client, server registry, document sync, diagnostics, hover, completion, Problems integration, status UI, and explicit fallback behavior as the foundation before navigation and chat enhancements.

items.title: Unavailable and network-loss recovery is not specified
items.statement: The core promises explicit fallback when no server is available and a bridge for TCP-only servers, but does not define detection latency, timeout classification, retry and backoff, reconnect/resync, duplicate process prevention, offline persistence, or recovery of views and pending requests after the server or bridge returns.
items.impact: Transient failure can strand the editor in stale fallback, cause reconnect storms, or replay requests against unsynchronized documents.
items.builder_discretion: Set retry timings, but specify bounded backoff, cancellation, single-owner reconnect, full resync, and user-visible recovery truth.

evidence.exact_quote: - Fallback when LSP unavailable

items.title: Pressure and lifecycle controls have no observability contract
items.statement: None of LSPS-027 through LSPS-033 defines metrics, structured events, support diagnostics, correlation identifiers, or redaction rules for document eviction, dropped/coalesced changes, bridge startup, timeouts, fallback transitions, partial results, approvals, and recovery.
items.impact: Operators and support cannot distinguish server defects, pressure controls, user-disabled state, bridge failure, or client races without exposing sensitive source content in ad hoc logs.
items.builder_discretion: Choose telemetry tooling, but require privacy-safe state-transition and failure signals with request and server correlation.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The LSP client controls scale pressure by limiting open documents per server, sending didClose on buffer eviction, capping initialize roots, debouncing didChange at the default interval, preferring incremental contentChanges when supported, and avoiding thousands of initialize paths.

items.title: Acceptance criteria validate migration traceability, not behavior
items.statement: Every unit in the core repeats audit-addressability and migration/index validation criteria, but supplies no executable oracle for scale caps, didClose, change ordering, fallback truth, bridge failure, status-envelope mapping, approval gating, phase outcomes, accessibility, or privacy. A structurally valid plan can pass while the normative behavior remains untested.
items.impact: Governance validation can report success without demonstrating any runtime contract in this window.
items.builder_discretion: Add unit, integration, fault-injection, security, and accessible-UI oracles tied to each normative behavior and negative constraint.

evidence.exact_quote: - The covered source span remains losslessly available for exact-text audit.

items.title: Legacy alias retirement lacks an input migration policy
items.statement: The core retires stale aliases and treats lsp_rename as a legacy alias, but does not define which stored requests, settings, scripts, or integrations continue to accept it, precedence when old and new names coexist, warnings, telemetry, removal version, or canonical serialization. The reader cannot tell whether legacy input remains compatible or is rejected.
items.impact: Existing callers may break abruptly or legacy names may persist indefinitely and create inconsistent authorization paths.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the deprecation interval, but specify accepted inputs, canonical output, conflict handling, warning, and removal criteria.

evidence.exact_quote: - The packetization label `10 read-only + 1 write-gated (lsp_rename)` is reconciled by treating `lsp_rename` as a legacy alias.

items.title: User-visible LSP states have no localization contract
items.statement: Problems, status UI, fallback, Settings > LSP, install hints, errors, partial results, and approvals are user-visible, yet the core does not define localization keys, parameterized messages, plural and length handling, locale-safe command presentation, or which protocol and server strings must remain unlocalized technical text.
items.impact: Implementations can hard-code English, truncate translated state labels, or interpolate untrusted server text unsafely.
items.builder_discretion: Choose copy, but require localizable keys, safe parameter separation, layout expansion, and a rule for protocol tokens.

evidence.exact_quote: - Settings > LSP

items.title: Concrete default scale constants are preserved
items.statement: The core preserves concrete reviewable values for the per-server open-document cap, initialize-root cap, and didChange debounce. These remove unlimited-growth ambiguity even though enforcement and exceedance behavior remain gaps.

evidence.exact_quote: - max 50 open docs per server
- capped at 10

items.title: Referenced owner contracts cannot be verified inside this blind window
items.statement: The core repeatedly says referenced owner documents retain SSOT boundaries, and specifically assigns fallback navigation to FileManager, but the authorized excerpt does not contain those owner contracts. It is therefore unknown whether FileManager, FileSafe, Chat, Problems, Settings, and Assistant consumers define matching envelopes, transitions, privacy, and recovery behavior.
items.impact: Seam compatibility cannot be certified from this assignment without violating the blind-window read boundary.
items.builder_discretion: None within this blind review; resolve in a later authorized cross-document seam phase.

evidence.exact_quote: - Plans/FileManager.md owns fallback symbol navigation; Plans/LSPSupport.md owns the LSP unavailable boundary.

dimension_assessments.summary: Eviction, fallback, status-envelope, and phase contracts do not enumerate notifications or consistent consumer behavior.
Fallback, eviction, reconnect, and phase transitions lack complete state machines and invalid-state handling.
Debounced edits, bridge port/process lifecycle, and approval-to-apply freshness expose races without serialization rules.
Eviction, bridge startup, partial result status, and multi-file writes lack partial-failure semantics.
Bridge/server recovery and rename rollback are not defined.
Install hints, bridge commands, and rename approvals lack origin, actor, scope, and immutable authorization bindings.
Chat and Assistant diagnostic context has no consent, minimization, transmission, retention, or deletion contract.
Install hints, custom bridge commands/endpoints, server responses, and diagnostic prompt content are not bounded as untrusted.
Fallback has one negative truth constraint, but complete stale, partial, disabled, loading, error, and recovery presentation remains absent.
Unavailable fallback exists, but timeout, bounded retry, reconnect, resync, and recovery behavior are not specified.
Concrete caps are preserved, but eviction selection, active-state protection, exceedance behavior, and bounded queues are absent.
Named status, Problems, Settings, fallback, and approval surfaces lack keyboard and assistive-technology semantics.
User-visible statuses, settings, hints, errors, and approvals lack localization and safe interpolation requirements.
Native TCP scope is clear, but legacy operation aliases and stored caller/settings migration are underdefined.
No privacy-safe telemetry or support-diagnostic contract covers pressure, lifecycle, fallback, bridge, envelope, or approval behavior.
FileSafe routing and approval gating are explicit non-gaps, but preview binding, atomicity, partial apply, and rollback remain unspecified.
The excerpt names owner boundaries but does not include the referenced FileManager, FileSafe, Chat, Problems, Settings, or Assistant contracts needed to certify seam compatibility.
Acceptance and validation surfaces prove lineage and structure rather than the runtime, security, failure, privacy, or GUI contracts.
Cross-owner contracts and their downstream behaviors are intentionally unavailable in this blind window, so no invented conclusion is made about them.
